unit-mismatch.title: Unit mismatch

realHistory.value: Mars Climate Orbiter, 1999: one team used English units, the other metric, for a key spacecraft operation, and the craft was lost.
realHistory.source: NASA/JPL news, "Mars Climate Orbiter Team Finds Likely Cause of Loss" (Sept. 30, 1999); read Nov 11, 2026

unit-mismatch.prompt: Navigation numbers from two teams don't quite agree. Check again?

options.label: Spend propellant on an extra navigation check

upside-down-sensor.title: Upside-down sensor

realHistory.value: Genesis, 2004: its deceleration sensors had been installed incorrectly, so the parachute never opened and the capsule crashed.
realHistory.source: NASA NSSDCA, Genesis ("The parachute never deployed"; "incorrectly installed accelerometers"); read Nov 11, 2026

upside-down-sensor.prompt: Before launch: the capsule's sensors have only been checked on paper. Pay for an extra test?

options.label: Pay for an extra test before launch

false-touchdown.title: False touchdown

realHistory.value: Mars Polar Lander, 1999: most likely a false signal that it had landed shut its engines off too early.
realHistory.source: NASA Science, Mars Polar Lander / Deep Space 2 (the investigation found it was most likely a false signal that the spacecraft had landed); read Nov 11, 2026

false-touchdown.prompt: Not used for orbiters; kept for future lander missions.

options.label: Add a software check that ignores early leg signals

memory-full.title: Memory full

realHistory.value: Spirit rover, 2004: too many files filled flash memory and caused reboots; fixed from Earth.
realHistory.source: NASA/JPL news, "Mars Rover Spirit Restored to Health" (2004: thousands of files deleted from flash memory; the computer had been resetting itself about once an hour); read Nov 11, 2026

memory-full.prompt: The onboard memory is full and the computer keeps rebooting.

lost-attitude.title: Lost attitude

realHistory.value: SOHO, 1998: lost attitude control and contact; recovered months later.
realHistory.source: SOHO (NASA/ESA), "A Diary of the Recovery" (contact lost June 24, 1998; re-established Aug. 3; attitude recovered Sept. 16); read Nov 11, 2026

lost-attitude.prompt: The craft is tumbling and has lost its lock on the Sun.

options.label: Spend propellant and power to recover now

powerMargin.source: Game estimate: power margin needed to run recovery

solar-storm.title: Solar storm

realHistory.value: Solar particle events can trigger spacecraft safe mode.
realHistory.source: Summary from general knowledge (spec); check against NASA LLIS before release

solar-storm.prompt: A solar particle storm is on its way.
